title: Per-model softlock and escrowed degradation plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background: We need a safer, more granular circuit-breaker approach that prevents wholesale denial-of-service for high-priority tenants and critical models while still protecting cluster SLOs. Existing per-tenant/model breakers trip fully and either route to generic fallbacks or hard-deny. That causes bad UX for paying customers and makes rollbacks noisy.

Proposal summary: Implement a 'softlock + escrow' pattern: when a breaker trips for a dependency/model/tenant, instead of fully closing the path we allocate a small, decaying escrow of tokens (softlock credit) that allows a bounded number of requests to continue to the primary model under strict constraints. Escrow behavior is weighted by tenant priority and model criticality, and requests consume escrow tokens in proportion to resource cost (estimated compute units). When escrow is exhausted, requests are routed to safe fallbacks defined per-model (cache, quantized variant, stubbed short answer, or queued retry).

Key ideas and differences from current breakers: 1) softlock credit pool per (region, model-version, tenant-cohort) with time-decay and configurable replenishment policy; 2) proportional consumption of escrow based on estimated tokens/latency; 3) graded fallbacks (tiered: cached response -> quantized model -> synthetic stub) with per-fallback quality and billing adjustments; 4) deterministic hysteresis windows to avoid flapping and thrash; 5) observability hooks to map escrow drain to SLO burn and billing events.

Why this helps: - Protects cluster SLOs and downstream dependencies while preserving partial service for high-value customers. - Gives ops fine-grained control for graceful degradation instead of abrupt cutoffs. - Enables prioritization of critical models (e.g., fraud detection) during regional capacity stress.

Design details: - Trip thresholds: use combined metrics (p95 latency, 5m error rate, cpu/gpu-steal) with configurable weights per dependency. Threshold formula: TripScore = w1*normalized(p95_latency) + w2*error_rate + w3*resource_pressure. Trip when TripScore > trip_threshold for window W. Default trip_threshold=0.8, W=60s. - Softlock sizing: escrow_initial = base_quanta * tenant_priority_multiplier * model_criticality_multiplier. Base_quanta derived from expected 95th percentile tokens/second for the model. Escrow decays exponentially with half-life H (default 120s) and optionally replenishes slowly if subsystem health improves. - Consumption model: each request consumes cost_estimate = ceil(request_tokens * model_cost_factor). For batched requests, cost is summed; concurrent requests compete for escrow via atomic token allocation. - Fallback ordering: each model registers an ordered fallback list. The runtime attempts each fallback until a response is returned or the final fallback is reached. Fallbacks must be registered with a quality tag (high/medium/low) and a max-tokens cap. - Hysteresis and cooldown: after escrow drains and breaker fully trips, a cooldown delay is enforced per (tenant, model) with exponential backoff before replenishment attempts. - Safety features: guaranteed transparent billing adjustments when fallback used (customers see that cheaper fallback used). Admin override APIs to force-break, force-pin, or donate escrow between tenants in emergencies.

Configuration surface: - Admin UI + API to set trip_threshold, weights, escrow base_quanta, half-life, tenant_priority mapping, fallback chains, and per-tenant caps. - Default templates: "enterprise-critical", "standard", "experimental" mapped to multipliers {2.0,1.0,0.2}.

Telemetry and SLO mapping: - Emit events: BreakerTripped, EscrowAllocated, EscrowConsumed, EscrowExhausted, FallbackInvoked({fallback_type}), EscrowReplenished, BreakerRecovered. - Tag events with model, model_version, tenant_id, region, and request_trace_id. - Dashboards: per-model escrow health, cumulative fallback rate, SLO burn per-tenant, and top consumers consuming escrow.

Operational constraints: - Implementation must be lock-free for the common path to avoid adding latency. Use atomic compare-and-swap on token counters and best-effort local caches for fast checks. - Fallback routing must be idempotent and respect request semantics (no side-effect-causing fallbacks for non-idempotent operations). - All configuration stored in control-plane with RBAC.

Out of scope for MVP: cross-region escrow donation (will be follow-up), advanced admission controllers, and deep ML-based cost estimators (use heuristic cost factors initially).
acceptance_criteria: Escrow allocation created per (tenant_cohort, model_version, region) when breaker trips
Request path can allocate and consume escrow tokens with <1ms median overhead on warm paths
Fallback chain is invoked deterministically when escrow exhausted and logged with reason code
Dashboard shows escrow levels and fallback rates per model within 5 minutes of events
SLO burn mapping: fallback invocation increases SLO-burn metric and is visible in alerts
Admin APIs exist to modify multipliers and to force-donate escrow between tenants
E2E tests that simulate dependency spike show graceful degradation for high-priority tenant and full cut for lowest-priority cohort
rollout_plan: Feature flag gated: start disabled cluster-wide, enable on single canary region
Phase 1: Enable softlock for non-critical experimental tenants and observe for 48h
Phase 2: Expand to standard tenants and enable dashboards/alerts, run 1-week soak
Phase 3: Enable for enterprise-critical with conservative multipliers and run two-week soak
Fallback: provide kill-switch that sets all escrows to zero and routes to hard fallbacks
Rollback: revert feature flag and drain escrows; monitor for SLO recovery within 5 minutes
telemetry: log: escrow.event (json) includes request_trace_id, reason_code, pre/post_token
test_plan: Unit: token accounting math and decay functions with deterministic clocks
Integration: simulate concurrent allocations from N=100 tenants against one model and assert no negative tokens and correctness under race
Chaos: inject synthetic latency/error spikes in dependency and verify fallback ordering and no request duplication
Performance: benchmark warm-path overhead across p95 and p99 under 1k rps
E2E: run canary in staging with production-like load and verify SLO burn behavior matches expectations
comments: 2026-02-21 - Aisha Patel: Initial proposal drafted after oncall incident where customer A lost access when regional GPU pool overloaded. Leaving open for architecture review.
2026-02-25 - Priya Rao (SRE): Architecture review notes: ensure fallback handlers are idempotent; prefer cache-first for read-only endpoints. Suggested adding an alert for escrow-donation requests.

2026-03-01 - Marcus Chen: Prototype of token accounting uploaded: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1897. Uses atomic counters and a sharded in-memory map per region. Benchmark shows +0.6ms median overhead. Needs optimization for p99.
2026-03-05 - Design review (Kenji Morita): UX for admin console sketched in Figma: https://www.figma.com/file/xyz/escrow-ui. Key ask: make per-tenant multipliers visible and editable with audit log.
2026-03-10 - Compliance (Lina Gomez): flagged storage of tenant multipliers as sensitive config; recommend encryption at rest in control-plane and audit trails (logged).
2026-03-12 - Marcus Chen: Implemented metrics and initial dashboard panels: link to Grafana: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/escrow/escrow-health. Ready for phase 1 canary in us-west-2.
